title: DECam Legacy Survey Announces Third Data Release
caption: The galaxy UGC 4640, imaged by the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope for the DECam Legacy Survey

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: This image of the galaxy UGC 4640, in the constellation Hydra, comes from the DECam Legacy Survey, known as DECaLS. The survey was carried out with the Dark Energy Camera on the CTIO Blanco telescope.

It accompanied the survey's third data release, which made processed images and catalogues of sources available, spanning somewhere between 4000 and 8000 square degrees of the sky, in three wavelength bands. Anyone can explore the survey images using its online sky viewer.

DECaLS is one of three public surveys that together will image 14,000 square degrees of sky. Their purpose is to supply targets for the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, a cosmology project at the Kitt Peak Mayall telescope. Large sky surveys like this record enormous numbers of galaxies, and individual objects such as UGC 4640 are captured along the way.

understand.summary: DECam on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope recorded this through g, r and z filters, spanning visible and near-infrared light. The source does not say which colour each filter was assigned.

understand.eye: The z band reaches into near-infrared light beyond the eye's range, and the survey camera records galaxies far too faint to see by eye.
